classification.difficultyReason: Combine rain and dry paths to find the overall win probability, then reverse the conditioning by dividing the rainy-win probability by the total win probability.

content.prompt: The manager of a team notices that the team has a probability of 0.6 of winning the game if it is raining, but 0.25 if it is dry. The probability that it will rain when they play is 0.3.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the probability that they will not win.

answer.worked:
Let $R$ be rain, $D$ be dry weather and $W$ be a win. The dry branch has probability $P(D)=1-0.3=0.7$. The probabilities of no win are $1-0.6=0.4$ on the rain branch and $1-0.25=0.75$ on the dry branch.

$$\begin{align*}P(W^c)&=P(R)P(W^c\mid R)+P(D)P(W^c\mid D)\\P(W^c)&=0.3\times0.4+0.7\times0.75\\P(W^c)&=0.120+0.525\\P(W^c)&=0.645\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Given that the team has won a game, calculate the probability that it rained on the day of the match. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

answer.short:
$0.507$

Divide the probability of a rainy win by the total probability of a win.
answer.worked:
Multiply along each winning branch, then add the two winning probabilities.

$$\begin{align*}P(R\cap W)&=0.3\times0.6\\P(R\cap W)&=0.180\\P(D\cap W)&=0.7\times0.25\\P(D\cap W)&=0.175\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}P(R\mid W)&=\frac{P(R\cap W)}{P(R\cap W)+P(D\cap W)}\\P(R\mid W)&=\frac{0.180}{0.180+0.175}\\P(R\mid W)&=\frac{36}{71}\\P(R\mid W)&\approx0.507\end{align*}$$
